protocol: 20 code cells, 2 surface pairs x 6 perturbation types = 12 conditions, 20 random 8/4 splits, Spearman rho of pairwise Euclidean distances
metric: total_variation_distance between surface pair readouts under each condition
transfer_test: Spearman correlation of cell-pair distances under train conditions vs test conditions
engagement_criterion: P(any digit) > 0.5 required for meaningful measurement

GPT2-small.note: noise floor - model does not understand code

Pythia-70M.note: noise floor - model does not understand code

Pythia-410M.note: noise floor - 0 active cells despite 40% accuracy

Phi-2.note: TOKENIZATION MISMATCH: model predicts newline (97.2%) not digits. P(any digit) ~ 0. Correctness is artifact of argmax among negligible probabilities.

key_findings: All 5 capable models (P(digit) > 0.99) show transfer rho in [0.04, 0.33] with real TV signal (>0.06)
Cross-family validated: SmolLM2-1.7B (HuggingFace) rho=0.042, Qwen models rho=0.12-0.33
All capable LLMs show rho below NK K=N-1 maximum (0.199-0.578) = super-maximal interaction complexity
Dramatically lower than biology: yeast 0.877, GB1 0.975
Within Qwen2.5 family: rho decreases with size (0.327 -> 0.235 -> 0.158)
Qwen3-1.7B (newer training) shows lower rho than Qwen2.5-3B (larger but older)
Model sensitivity (max TV) does NOT predict transfer rho: Qwen2.5-0.5B has highest TV (0.169) but highest rho (0.327)
Incapable models (<50% correct or P(digit)~0) show inflated rho from noise-floor correlation
Phi-2 tokenization incompatibility: predicts newline not digits, so readout doesn't engage
interpretation: Language processing has super-maximal interaction complexity (effective K > N-1). All capable models that faithfully process language inherit this property. This is a fundamental limit on finite-testing behavioral verification: training-condition behavior does NOT predict held-out behavior.
